tasks.title: Add rate limiting and input sanitization to API endpoints
tasks.description: Implement a request‑rate‑limiting middleware (e.g., express‑rate‑limit) in server.js to protect public endpoints from brute‑force and DoS attacks. Add a validation layer using a schema library (e.g., Joi) in src/lib/db.js and route handlers to sanitize and validate all incoming parameters (search queries, booking dates, user IDs). acceptance: Database connections are reused; the number of active connections never exceeds the pool size (e.g., 20).
Cache hit rate for listings is at least 60% in load tests.
Response time for GET /listings drops by ≥30% compared to baseline (measured with a simple load test).

tasks.title: 5'li Arayüz ve Tasarım Süper Paketi (Map Clustering, Lightbox, Dark Mode, AI Recommendations, Lazy Loading)
tasks.description:
Implement the complete 5-feature Frontend & Design suite in a single integrated PR:
1. Leaflet Map Clustering: Cluster listing markers into number bubbles when zoomed out (< 13); smooth zoom on click; individual price badges when zoomed in.
2. 5-Photo Grid & Lightbox: Airbnb standard 1 large + 4 small photo grid on ListingDetail.jsx; click opens full-screen accessible Lightbox modal with keyboard navigation (ESC, arrow keys).
3. Dark / Light Mode Toggle: Smooth animated sun/moon theme switch button on Navbar.jsx; persist in localStorage; apply Tailwind dark: styles across all cards and modals.
4. AI-Powered Recommendations Carousel: RecommendationCarousel.jsx on home page showing smart matching listings based on category & viewed listings.
5. Responsive & Lazy-Load Images: Add loading="lazy" and responsive srcset across ListingCard.jsx, ListingDetail.jsx, and ExperienceCard.jsx.
acceptance: 1. Map Clustering: Zooming out clusters listing markers; clicking zooms into the cluster area smoothly.
2. Photo Lightbox: 5-photo grid renders on detail page; clicking any image opens full-screen gallery with ESC/arrow key controls.
3. Theme Switcher: Theme button toggles between light and dark modes with persistent localStorage state.
4. Recommendation Carousel: Matching listings carousel renders on home page without layout shifts.
5. Lazy Loading: Off-screen images have loading="lazy" and load on demand as user scrolls.
6. Test Coverage: All tests in tests/frontend_design_suite.test.js pass cleanly with 0 failures.

tasks.title: Web Push Notification Engine for Real‑time Guest/Host Alerts
tasks.description: Implement a fullstack push notification system. Add a new SQLite table `push_subscriptions` with columns `id`, `userId`, `endpoint`, `keysP`, `keysAuth`. Create `src/lib/pushNotificationEngine.js` exposing `saveSubscription(userId, subscription)`, `removeSubscription(userId)`, and `sendNotification(userId, payload)` using the `web-push` library with VAPID keys. Extend `server.js` with two REST endpoints: POST /api/notifications/subscribe (auth‑protected, stores subscription) and POST /api/notifications/unsubscribe (removes subscription). Update booking and chat logic (e.g., after `insertMessage` and after `insertBooking` status change) to call `sendNotification` with appropriate payloads. On the frontend, add `src/components/PushNotificationProvider.jsx` that registers a service worker (`src/service-worker.js`), requests Notification permission, and posts the subscription to the backend. The service worker listens for `push` events and displays a notification with title/body from the payload. Update `App.jsx` to wrap the app with `<PushNotificationProvider>` and display a UI toggle in the user settings menu.
acceptance: A logged‑in user can enable notifications in the UI, the browser shows the permission prompt, and the subscription is persisted in the SQLite `push_subscriptions` table.
When a new chat message is inserted for that user, a push notification appears on the device even if the browser tab is closed.

tasks.title: Interactive Map Clustering for Listings
tasks.description: Implement a geospatial clustering feature for the map view. Add a new GET endpoint `/api/map/listings` in server.js that accepts `bbox` (minLng,minLat,maxLng,maxLat) query parameters and returns listings inside the bounding box with a geohash precision based on zoom level. Create a new library module `src/lib/mapEngine.js` that computes geohash clusters and aggregates listing counts. Extend `src/lib/db.js` with a helper `getListingsInBBox(minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat)` that uses an indexed SQLite R-Tree for fast spatial queries. Update the frontend `src/components/MapView.jsx` to request clustered data, and add a new component `src/components/MapCluster.jsx` that renders cluster markers (showing count) and individual listing markers when zoomed in. Ensure clicking a cluster zooms the map to its bounds. All code should include input validation, proper error handling, and use existing JWT auth middleware for protected access.
acceptance: GET /api/map/listings with a valid bbox returns a JSON array of cluster objects (geohash, count, centroid) and individual listings when zoom level is high.
MapView displays cluster markers with correct counts and expands to individual markers on zoom in.
Clicking a cluster marker smoothly zooms the map to the cluster's bounding box.
All responses respect authentication and return 401 for unauthenticated requests.

tasks.title: Instant Booking Approval Flow
tasks.description: Add a host‑side approval workflow for instant‑booking requests. Extend the GraphQL schema with a new mutation `approveBooking(id: ID!, approved: Boolean!): Booking` and a subscription `bookingStatusChanged(hostId: ID!): Booking`. Implement the resolver in `src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js` and the business logic in `src/lib/bookingEngine.js` to update booking status, send a push notification, and log the action. Create a new UI component `src/components/BookingApprovalModal.jsx` that lists pending instant‑booking requests for the logged‑in host, shows listing details, and lets the host approve or reject with an optional message. Wire the component into `HostDashboard` and ensure the GraphQL client updates the UI via the subscription. Add necessary DB fields (`approvedAt`, `approvalStatus`) to the `bookings` table in `src/lib/db.js` and migrate existing data. Ensure proper authorization checks using `authMiddleware`.
acceptance: Host dashboard shows a badge with the count of pending instant‑booking requests.
Clicking a request opens BookingApprovalModal with correct listing info and approve/reject buttons.
Approving a request updates the booking status to `approved`, sets `approvedAt`, and triggers a GraphQL subscription that updates the guest UI in real time.
Rejecting a request updates the status to `rejected`, stores the host's optional message, and notifies the guest via push notification.
Unauthorized users cannot invoke the approveBooking mutation; attempts return a 403 error.

tasks.title: Host Payout & Revenue Analytics Dashboard
tasks.description: Implement a secure host payout system and analytics dashboard. Add a new SQLite table for payouts and corresponding CRUD helpers in src/lib/db.js (createPayout, getPayoutsByHost, getHostRevenueSummary). Create a payoutEngine module (src/lib/payoutEngine.js) that calculates host earnings from bookings, applies fees, and schedules payouts. Extend the GraphQL schema (src/lib/graphqlSchema.js) and resolvers (src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js) with queries getHostRevenueSummary and mutation requestPayout. Add a REST endpoint /api/hosts/:hostId/payouts in server.js that returns JSON and supports CSV export via a query param. Build a React component HostPayoutDashboard.jsx under src/components that displaying total earnings, pending payouts, and a paginated payout history, and integrate it as a new tab in HostDashboard.jsx. Protect all new endpoints with authMiddleware so only the authenticated host can access their own data.
acceptance: Host can view a dashboard showing total earnings, pending payouts, and payout history with correct calculations.
API endpoint /api/hosts/:hostId/payouts returns JSON of payouts filtered by host and respects auth.
CSV export via ?format=csv returns a correctly formatted file with payout records.
All new code passes existing unit tests and linting.

tasks.title: Web Push Notification Engine for Real‑time Guest/Host Alerts
tasks.description: Add a complete Web Push workflow: generate VAPID keys, create src/lib/pushEngine.js that uses the web-push library to send notifications, store subscriptions in a new SQLite table via db.js, expose POST /api/push/subscribe in server.js to receive the browser subscription, and add a React context component (src/components/PushNotificationProvider.jsx) that registers the service worker, requests permission, and subscribes the user. Also add a NotificationBell UI component (src/components/NotificationBell.jsx) that shows an unread badge and opens a toast when a push payload arrives. Hook the push trigger into existing booking and chat events (e.g., after insertMessage and after booking confirmation) so hosts and guests receive instant alerts.
acceptance: POST /api/push/subscribe stores the subscription in the SQLite subscriptions table and returns HTTP 200
When a new chat message is inserted, the server calls pushEngine.sendNotification and the subscribed client receives a push event that displays a toast and increments the NotificationBell badge
Service worker (public/sw.js) correctly handles the push event and shows a notification with the provided title and body

tasks.title: iCal Calendar Sync for Listings
tasks.description: Add iCal feed generation for each listing so hosts can subscribe to a calendar URL that reflects all confirmed bookings. Implement a new Express route GET /api/listings/:id/ical that returns a valid .ics file. Create src/lib/calendarSync.js with a function generateIcs(listingId) that queries confirmed bookings from the DB, formats them using the ical-generator package, and caches the result for 2 minutes. Update src/lib/db.js with a helper getConfirmedBookingsForListing(listingId). Secure the endpoint with a signed token (hostId + secret) passed as query param token, validated by authMiddleware. Ensure the iCal feed updates automatically when a booking status changes (hook into updateBookingStatus to invalidate cache).
acceptance: GET /api/listings/:id/ical?token=validToken returns a 200 response with Content-Type text/calendar and contains VEVENT entries for each confirmed booking of that listing.
When a booking is created, cancelled, or its status changes, the iCal feed reflects the change within 2 minutes (cache invalidation works).

tasks.title: Host Payout & Revenue Analytics Dashboard
tasks.description: Add a full‑stack host payout and revenue analytics capability. Extend the SQLite schema with a `payouts` table (id, hostId, amount, currency, periodStart, periodEnd, status, createdAt). Implement a payoutEngine library that aggregates confirmed bookings per host, calculates commissions, taxes and net payout, and writes payout records. Expose GraphQL queries `hostPayouts(hostId, from, to)` and `hostRevenueSummary(hostId, year)` and mutations `triggerPayout(hostId, month)`. Update server.js to register the new resolvers and add a DataLoader for efficient host‑by‑id fetching. Create a React component `HostPayoutDashboard` that fetches the data via the GraphQL endpoint, displays a table of monthly payouts, a summary chart of gross vs net revenue, and a button to trigger a new payout. Integrate the component into `App.jsx` under a new route/view `host_payouts`. Ensure all inputs are validated and sanitized, and that the API is protected by the existing authMiddleware.
acceptance: Database contains a `payouts` table with the correct columns and indexes.
GraphQL schema includes `hostPayouts`, `hostRevenueSummary`, and `triggerPayout` fields with proper type definitions.
Calling `triggerPayout` for a host creates a new payout record with accurate gross, commission, tax, and net amounts.
The `HostPayoutDashboard` component renders a paginated list of payouts and a revenue summary chart for the logged‑in host.
Only authenticated hosts can access the payout dashboard; unauthenticated requests receive an authorization error.
All new code passes linting and existing unit tests without regression.

tasks.title: Guest Review Moderation Dashboard
tasks.description: Add a full moderation workflow for guest reviews. Extend the GraphQL schema with queries to fetch pending reviews and mutations to approve or reject a review (including an optional moderationReason). Implement resolver logic in src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js and DB helper functions in src/lib/db.js to update the reviews table (status, moderationReason) and emit a notification via src/lib/notifications.js. Create a new React component src/components/ReviewModerationPanel.jsx that displays pending reviews, provides Approve/Reject buttons, and shows a textarea for the reason. Guard the GraphQL endpoints with authMiddleware so only users with admin role can access. Register the new resolvers in server.js and ensure rate limiting is applied via the existing rate limiter.
acceptance: Admin user can open the Review Moderation Panel and see a list of reviews with status 'pending'.
Clicking Approve changes the review status to 'published', removes it from the pending list, and sends a notification to the reviewer.
Clicking Reject updates the review status to 'rejected', stores the entered moderationReason, removes it from the pending list, and sends a notification to the reviewer.
GraphQL query `pendingReviews` returns only reviews with status 'pending'.
GraphQL mutations `approveReview(id)` and `rejectReview(id, reason)` correctly modify the DB and return the updated review object.
All actions are blocked for non‑admin users (401 Unauthorized).
Rate limiting is enforced on the moderation mutations (no more than 10 requests per minute per admin).

tasks.title: AI‑Powered Concierge Chat Integration
tasks.description: Add a real‑time AI concierge service that answers guest and host questions. Implement a new GraphQL mutation `requestAiResponse(message: String!): AiMessage!` in `server.js` that forwards the prompt to the diffusion‑LLM endpoint (via a new helper `src/lib/aiConcierge.js`). Store each exchange in the existing chat engine tables (`messages` table) using `insertMessage` and retrieve history with `getMessagesForListing`. Extend `src/lib/chatEngine.js` to expose `requestAiResponse` and a DataLoader for chat history. Update the UI component `src/components/MagdaConciergeWidget.jsx` to call the mutation, display a loading spinner, and render the AI response in the chat window. Ensure the widget shows the full conversation on open and persists across page reloads. Add basic input sanitization and rate‑limit the mutation using the existing rate‑limiter.
acceptance: When a user types a query in the Magda Concierge widget and presses send, the UI shows a loading indicator and then displays an AI‑generated answer within 2 seconds.
All sent and received messages appear in the chat window and are persisted; re‑opening the widget after a page reload shows the full conversation history.
The GraphQL mutation `requestAiResponse` returns a non‑empty `AiMessage` object and respects the global rate‑limit (max 10 requests per minute per user).

tasks.title: Add GraphQL Subscriptions for Real‑time Booking & Notification Updates
tasks.description: Extend the GraphQL API to support WebSocket‑based subscriptions so that clients receive immediate updates when a booking status changes or a new notification is created. Implement a new Subscription type in src/lib/graphqlSchema.js, resolver logic in src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js, and a WebSocket server in server.js using the graphql‑ws library. Hook the subscription publish calls into existing booking status updates (updateBookingStatus) and notification creation (saveNotification) in src/lib/notifications.js. Ensure the server upgrades HTTP requests to WS on the same endpoint and that authentication middleware validates the JWT on the WS connection.
acceptance: A client can open a subscription to bookingUpdates and receives a payload with the updated booking object immediately after updateBookingStatus is called.
A client can subscribe to userNotifications and receives a new notification object instantly when saveNotification is invoked.

tasks.title: Multi‑Currency Checkout Support
tasks.description: Implement end‑to‑end multi‑currency handling for booking payments. Extend the payment engine to accept a currency code, convert prices using a live FX service, and store amounts in both the booking currency and the host's preferred currency. Update GraphQL mutations for createBooking and processPayment to accept a `currency` argument. Add a UI selector in the CheckoutModal component, persist the chosen currency in user settings, and display formatted amounts throughout the UI. Modify src/lib/currencyEngine.js to expose `convertAmount(amount, from, to)` using an external rates API (e.g., exchangerate.host). Ensure all new fields (priceCurrency, convertedPrice, exchangeRate) are persisted in the SQLite bookings table via a migration in src/lib/db.js.
acceptance: A new column `priceCurrency` and `convertedPrice` are added to the bookings table and populated on booking creation.
The CheckoutModal shows a dropdown of supported currencies (USD, EUR, TRY, GBP) and updates the displayed total price instantly after selection.
GraphQL mutation `createBooking(input: BookingInput!, currency: Currency!): Booking!` returns the booking with both original and converted amounts.
Payments processed through iyzico are sent in the selected currency and the transaction record stores the exchange rate used.

End‑to‑end test: create a booking in EUR, verify the SQLite row contains `priceCurrency='EUR'`, `convertedPrice` matches the host's currency after conversion, and the UI shows the correct formatted amount.

tasks.title: Guest Identity Verification via Document Upload and OCR
tasks.description: Add a secure document upload endpoint (POST /api/verify-id) that accepts image/PDF files, stores them in a protected folder, and invokes an OCR service (e.g., Tesseract via a child process) to extract the guest's name and document number. Extend the users table with columns `idVerificationStatus` (enum: pending, approved, rejected) and `idDocumentPath`. Create a new GraphQL mutation `requestIdVerification(file: Upload!): VerificationResult` and a query `userVerificationStatus(userId: ID!): VerificationStatus`. Implement a React component `IdentityVerificationModal` that allows guests to upload their ID, shows upload progress, and displays the verification result badge on the profile page. Update the auth middleware to block certain actions (e.g., booking) for users with `idVerificationStatus !== 'approved'`. Add server‑side rate limiting on the upload endpoint and sanitize file names. Store OCR results in a new table `id_verifications` with fields `userId`, `extractedName`, `extractedNumber`, `createdAt`. Ensure the upload directory is not served publicly.
acceptance: Uploading a valid ID image returns a pending status and creates a file in the secure uploads folder.
OCR extraction stores the extracted name and number in the `id_verifications` table and updates `users.idVerificationStatus` to 'approved' when the extracted name matches the user's profile name.
The profile page shows a green verification badge only after status is 'approved'.
Attempts to create a booking while status is not 'approved' are rejected with a clear error message.

tasks.title: Progressive Web App (PWA) Enablement for Airbnb Clone

tasks.title: Automated Payment Fraud Detection Engine
tasks.description: Create a fraud detection module that evaluates each payment request before it is sent to iyzico. Add a new `fraud_score` column to the `payments` table, implement `src/lib/fraudEngine.js` with rule‑based checks (e.g., velocity, mismatched IP/geo, blacklisted cards) and a simple ML scoring stub. Extend `src/lib/iyzicoEngine.js` to call `calculateFraudScore` during `processDirectPayment`, store the score in the DB, and abort the transaction if the score exceeds a configurable threshold (default 80). Update GraphQL resolvers to expose `fraudScore` on the `Payment` type and add a new `paymentFraudCheck` mutation for manual re‑evaluation. Ensure all new code is covered by unit tests and that the existing payment flow remains unchanged for low‑risk scores.
acceptance: A new column `fraud_score` exists in the `payments` table and is populated on every payment insert.
Payments with a fraud score > 80 are rejected and the API returns a `FraudDetected` error message.
The GraphQL schema includes `fraudScore` on the `Payment` type and the `paymentFraudCheck` mutation works as expected.
Unit tests in `src/lib/__tests__/fraudEngine.test.js` pass with >90% coverage.
No regression in existing payment processing tests.

tasks.title: AI‑Powered Personalized Listings Recommendation Engine
tasks.description: Introduce a new recommendation service that suggests listings to guests based on their past bookings, search history, and similar users. Add a `src/lib/recommendationEngine.js` module that loads a pre‑computed similarity matrix (SQLite table `user_similarity`) and provides `getRecommendedListings(userId, limit)`. Extend the GraphQL schema (`src/lib/graphqlSchema.js`) with a `recommendedListings(userId: ID!, limit: Int = 10): [Listing]` field and implement its resolver in `src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js` calling the new engine. Update `server.js` to expose the resolver via the existing GraphQL handler. Add a simple in‑memory LRU cache (NodeCache) to memoize results per user for 5 minutes. Ensure the new query respects existing auth middleware and rate limiting.
acceptance: GraphQL query `recommendedListings(userId: "usr_guest_01", limit: 5)` returns an array of up to 5 listing objects with correct fields.
Cache hit is verified by checking that a second identical query within 5 minutes does not trigger a new DB read (use console log or mock to confirm).

tasks.title: Host Performance Dashboard
tasks.description: Create a new host‑focused performance dashboard. Add GraphQL types, queries and resolvers to expose metrics such as response time, acceptance rate, booking conversion, average rating and total earnings. Implement DB helper functions to calculate these aggregates efficiently (using indexes and cached reads). Build a React component (HostPerformanceDashboard.jsx) that fetches the data via GraphQL and renders interactive charts using Recharts. Update navigation to include a "Performance" tab in the host dashboard and protect the route with existing auth middleware.
acceptance: Visiting the host dashboard shows a "Performance" tab that renders charts with correct numeric values matching the data in the SQLite DB.
The GraphQL endpoint returns a "hostPerformance" object with fields responseTimeMs, acceptanceRate, conversionRate, averageRating, totalEarnings for the authenticated host.

tasks.title: Fuzzy Full‑Text Search for Listings
tasks.description: Add SQLite FTS5 virtual table for listings (title, description, location). Populate / sync it on insert/update/delete. Extend GraphQL schema with a `searchListings(query: String!, limit: Int = 20): [Listing]` query that performs a fuzzy match using the FTS5 `bm25` ranking. Implement resolver in `src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js` that calls a new `searchListings` function in `src/lib/db.js`. Update the React UI (e.g., `CategoryBar` or a new `SearchBar` component) to call this GraphQL query as the user types, debounce input, and display results ordered by relevance. Ensure the search works with partial words and typo tolerance.
acceptance: Running `npm test` (or the project's test suite) passes a new test that verifies `searchListings('villa')` returns listings with 'villa' in title or description, ordered by relevance.
Manual verification: typing a misspelled term like 'vila' in the search UI returns relevant listings, and the results list updates after a 300 ms debounce.

tasks.title: Secure Photo Upload with Virus Scanning and Image Optimization
tasks.description: Add a new multipart/form-data endpoint (/api/listings/:id/photos) in server.js that uses multer for file handling. Pipe each uploaded file through a ClamAV scan (via node-clam) and reject the request if a virus is detected. On successful scan, process the image with sharp to create a 200x200 thumbnail and a web‑optimized JPEG (quality 80). Store the original and thumbnail in a public/uploads directory and record their URLs in the listings table (new columns photoUrl and thumbnailUrl). Expose a helper in src/lib/photoUpload.js for the upload, scan, and resize pipeline. Create a React component src/components/PhotoUpload.jsx that allows drag‑and‑drop or file‑picker selection, shows preview thumbnails, validates file type/size client‑side, and calls the new endpoint via fetch with the auth token. Update the HostDashboard and ListingDetail pages to include this component for creating/editing listings.
acceptance: Uploading a valid JPEG/PNG results in a new DB row with photoUrl and thumbnailUrl, files saved on disk, and the UI displays the thumbnail preview.
Uploading a file that fails the ClamAV scan returns a 400 response with an error message, no files are stored, and the DB is unchanged.
The PhotoUpload component rejects files >5 MB or non‑image MIME types before sending, and shows an appropriate validation message.

tasks.title: Multi‑Factor Authentication (MFA) for Guest & Host Accounts
tasks.description: Introduce optional time‑based one‑time password (TOTP) MFA. Add a new DB column `mfaEnabled` and `mfaSecret` to the users table. Extend the auth middleware to require a valid `x-mfa-token` header when `mfaEnabled` is true. Implement endpoints `POST /api/auth/mfa/setup` (generates a secret, returns QR code data URL) and `POST /api/auth/mfa/verify` (validates a TOTP code and issues a new JWT). Update `src/lib/auth.js` to include `verifyMfaToken` helper, modify `server.js` to mount the new routes, and adjust login flow to flag `mfaPending` in the JWT payload when MFA is required. Add unit tests in `src/tests/auth.mfa.test.js` to cover setup, verification, and login with MFA.
acceptance: User can enable MFA via /api/auth/mfa/setup and receives a QR code data URL.
Login for a user with MFA enabled returns a JWT with mfaPending flag and no access token until a valid TOTP is posted to /api/auth/mfa/verify.
All existing non‑MFA login flows remain unchanged.

tasks.title: Host Earnings Forecast Dashboard
tasks.description: Add a new analytics engine that aggregates upcoming bookings, dynamic pricing adjustments, and historical payout data to compute a 30‑day earnings forecast for each host. Extend the SQLite schema with a `host_forecasts` table, implement CRUD functions in `src/lib/analyticsEngine.js`, expose a GraphQL query `hostEarningsForecast(hostId: ID!): Forecast` in `src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js`, and update the GraphQL schema accordingly. Create a new React component `HostEarningsForecast.jsx` that fetches the forecast via the GraphQL endpoint, renders a line chart using a charting library (e.g., Recharts), and integrates it into the existing `HostDashboard` view. The forecast should be recomputed nightly via a scheduled job in `server.js` and cached in memory for fast retrieval.
acceptance: GraphQL query `hostEarningsForecast` returns a JSON object with fields `dates`, `projectedEarnings`, and `currency` for a given hostId.
The `HostEarningsForecast` component displays a line chart matching the returned data and updates automatically after the nightly recomputation job runs.

tasks.title: Bulk Listing Import via CSV
tasks.description: Add a new secure CSV import workflow that allows hosts to upload a CSV file containing multiple listings. Implement a POST /api/listings/import endpoint in server.js that validates the JWT, checks host role, and streams the uploaded file to a new library src/lib/csvImport.js. In csvImport.js, use fast-csv to parse rows, validate each against the existing Joi listingSchema, and insert listings in a single transaction using the existing insertListing function. Return a JSON summary with counts of successfully imported listings and detailed error messages for rows that failed validation. Update the GraphQL schema to expose a mutation importListingsFromCsv that triggers the same logic for API‑first consumers. Ensure the endpoint respects existing rate‑limiting and input‑sanitization middleware.
acceptance: Uploading a well‑formed CSV with 5 valid rows results in 5 new listings in the DB and a response { success: true, imported: 5, errors: [] }.
Uploading a CSV with 2 valid rows and 1 row missing required fields returns { success: false, imported: 2, errors: [{ row: 3, message: "hostId is required" }] } and no partial data is left in the DB.

tasks.title: Smart‑Lock Self‑Check‑In Integration
tasks.description: Add end‑to‑end support for generating one‑time access codes for smart‑lock devices. Create a new lockEngine module with functions generateAccessCode(listingId, bookingId) and revokeAccessCode(lockId, code). Extend the DB schema (src/lib/db.js) with a locks table (id, listingId, lockProvider, lockExternalId, lastCode, lastCodeExpires). Update the booking flow (src/lib/bookingEngine.js) to call generateAccessCode after payment confirmation and store the code. Add a new GraphQL mutation `createLockAccessCode(listingId, bookingId): AccessCodePayload`. Modify server.js to expose the mutation via the GraphQL handler. In the frontend, add a "Show Access Code" button in the BookingConfirmation component (src/components/BookingConfirmation.jsx) that fetches the code via the new mutation and displays it in a modal. Ensure the code is sent via the existing push‑notification engine (src/lib/notificationEngine.js).
acceptance: Database contains a new `locks` table with the correct columns.
After a successful booking payment, the GraphQL mutation `createLockAccessCode` returns a 6‑digit code and an expiration timestamp.
The BookingConfirmation UI shows a "Show Access Code" button that opens a modal displaying the code and expiry.
The generated code is sent as a push notification to the guest device.
Calling the mutation with an invalid listingId or bookingId returns a GraphQL error.

tasks.title: Host Payout & Revenue Analytics Dashboard
tasks.description: Create a new host‑focused dashboard that visualizes payout history, upcoming payouts, earnings breakdown by month, occupancy rates, and commission fees. Add a GraphQL type HostPayout and resolvers (getHostPayouts, getHostEarningsSummary) in src/lib/graphqlSchema.js and src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js. Extend the SQLite schema in src/lib/db.js with a payouts table if missing, and provide CRUD helpers. Implement React components (HostDashboard.jsx, RevenueChart.jsx, EarningsSummary.jsx) that fetch data via the GraphQL endpoint, cache results with NodeCache, and render interactive charts using Recharts. Protect the new /host/earnings route with authMiddleware and CSRF middleware in server.js, and expose it through Express static fallback for SSR. Update rate limiting to include the new endpoint.
acceptance: Visiting /host/earnings as an authenticated host displays a dashboard with total earnings, a monthly earnings chart, and upcoming payout amount.
GraphQL query getHostPayouts returns correct payout records for a host with mock entries in the SQLite database.
Dashboard updates automatically after a new booking is confirmed (via WebSocket or polling) without a full page reload.

tasks.title: Host Pricing Simulation Sandbox
tasks.description: Create a sandbox where hosts can input hypothetical occupancy rates, seasonal factors, and demand intensity to see projected nightly prices and revenue. Add a new GraphQL query `simulatePricing(listingId: ID!, occupancyRate: Float!, month: Int!, demandIntensity: String!): PricingSimulationResult!` that calls the existing `calculateDynamicPrice` engine and returns recommended price, multipliers, and projected monthly revenue (price * days * occupancyRate). Extend the GraphQL schema and resolver, add a new SQLite view or temporary table if needed for historical occupancy data, and implement a React component `PricingSimulator.jsx` under `src/components/` that renders a form, calls the new query via `graphql-request`, and displays a chart of projected revenue. Update `server.js` to expose the new query and ensure proper input validation with Joi. Add unit tests for the resolver and integration test for the UI flow.
acceptance: The PricingSimulator UI loads for a host, accepts occupancyRate, month, and demandIntensity, and displays a table with recommended nightly price, multipliers, and projected monthly revenue.

The GraphQL query `simulatePricing` returns correct calculations matching the `calculateDynamicPrice` output for given inputs and integrates with the existing pricing engine without breaking other queries.

tasks.title: Semantic Search with Vector Embeddings
tasks.description: Add a natural‑language search capability that matches listings based on semantic meaning rather than keyword matching. Implement a new module src/lib/searchEngine.js that loads a pre‑trained sentence‑transformer model (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2) via @xenova/transformers, generates a 384‑dimensional embedding for each listing description and title, and stores the embeddings as BLOBs in a new SQLite table (listings_embeddings). Extend server.js to expose a GraphQL query `semanticSearch(query: String!, limit: Int = 10): [Listing]` that computes the query embedding, performs a cosine‑similarity search against the stored embeddings using an in‑memory approximate nearest‑neighbor library (e.g., Annoy or a simple linear scan for <=10k rows), and returns the top‑N listings sorted by similarity. Update src/lib/graphqlSchema.js and src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js to wire the resolver. Add a background job that re‑embeds listings on create/update via a new function `updateListingEmbedding(listingId)` called from existing insertListing and updateListing functions. Ensure the new endpoint respects existing auth middleware and rate limiting.
acceptance: Calling the GraphQL query `semanticSearch(query: "beach house with pool", limit: 5)` returns at least one listing whose title or description contains a beach and a pool, and the results are ordered by decreasing cosine similarity.
The semantic search query for a dataset of 5,000 listings completes in ≤ 200 ms on the CI test runner, and the embedding table is correctly populated after inserting a new listing.

tasks.title: Faceted Search & Filter Engine
tasks.description: Add a faceted search capability that lets guests filter listings by price range, amenities, host type, rating, and location. Extend the SQLite schema with indexed columns for price, rating, and a JSON column for amenities. Create src/lib/searchEngine.js exposing a function searchListings(filters, pagination) that builds dynamic SQL with WHERE clauses and returns total count + rows. Add GraphQL fields `searchListings(filters: SearchInput, pagination: PaginationInput): SearchResult` and resolvers in src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js. Update server.js to register the new resolver. In the UI, add a filter panel component (e.g., src/components/FilterPanel.jsx) and integrate it into App.jsx and ListingGrid, wiring the UI controls to call the GraphQL search query via the existing GraphQL client. Ensure the filter state persists in URL query params and that the listing grid updates reactively.
acceptance: When a user selects a price range, amenities, and rating in the filter panel, the listing grid displays only listings that match all criteria and the URL contains the corresponding query parameters.
A GraphQL query `searchListings` with filter arguments returns a correct totalCount and a paginated list of listings that match the filters, verified by unit tests against the SQLite DB.

tasks.title: Video Chat Integration for Host‑Guest Communication
tasks.description: Add a WebRTC‑based video chat feature that lets a host and a guest start a live video call from the listing detail page. Implement a signaling server using Socket.io in server.js, create a lightweight wrapper in src/lib/videoChat.js for peer connection handling, and build a React modal component src/components/VideoChatModal.jsx that displays local and remote video streams. Extend the existing ChatModal UI to include a "Start Video Call" button that opens VideoChatModal. Ensure proper cleanup of streams on modal close and handle ICE candidate exchange via the Socket.io channel.
acceptance: From a listing detail view, clicking "Start Video Call" opens a modal with two video elements (local and remote).
When both parties accept, video streams are displayed with <2 seconds latency and no console errors.
Closing the modal stops the MediaStream and removes the Socket.io listeners.
The feature works across different browsers (Chrome, Firefox) and network configurations (NAT traversal).

tasks.title: Host Real‑Time Availability Dashboard
tasks.description: Add a new dashboard for hosts that displays all of their listings with current availability status and upcoming bookings. Implement a GraphQL query (or REST endpoint) in server.js that aggregates listing, booking, and calendarSyncStatus data from the SQLite DB via src/lib/db.js. Create a React component src/components/HostAvailabilityDashboard.jsx that fetches this data, renders a table of listings with columns for title, status, next available date, and a mini‑calendar showing booked dates. Integrate the component into src/App.jsx under the "host_dashboard" view. Ensure the dashboard updates when new bookings are created or calendar sync status changes.
acceptance: Visiting the Host Dashboard shows a table listing all host's listings with correct availability status and next free date.
Clicking a listing opens a mini‑calendar that highlights booked dates fetched from the DB.
When a new booking is added via the existing booking flow, the dashboard reflects the updated availability without a page reload.

tasks.title: Instant Booking Approval Flow
tasks.description: Add support for hosts to enable instant booking on a per‑listing basis and automatically confirm guest bookings when the flag is set. Update the DB schema to add a boolean `instantApproval` column to the `listings` table. Extend `src/lib/db.js` with a migration and helper `setInstantApproval(listingId, enabled)`. Modify `src/lib/bookingEngine.js` to check the listing's `instantApproval` flag during booking creation and set the booking status to `confirmed` automatically. Add a toggle UI in `src/components/HostDashboard.jsx` (or a new `InstantBookingToggle` component) that calls a new POST `/api/listings/:id/instant-approval` endpoint. Implement the endpoint in `server.js` with proper validation and auth middleware. Update `src/lib/notifications.js` to send a real‑time notification to the host and a confirmation email to the guest when an instant booking occurs. Ensure the frontend reflects the new status in `BookingWidget.jsx` (show "Instantly confirmed" badge).
acceptance: Host can toggle instant booking on a listing in the dashboard and the DB column `instantBooking` is updated accordingly.
When a guest books a listing with instant booking enabled, the booking is created with status `confirmed` without manual approval.
Host receives a notification about the new instant booking and the guest receives a confirmation email.
The booking widget displays an "Instantly confirmed" badge for bookings approved via instant booking.

tasks.title: Interactive Map Clustering for Listings
tasks.description: Add server‑side support for map clustering and update the map UI to display clusters. Implement a new endpoint `/api/listings/cluster` that accepts bounding box and zoom level, queries the SQLite DB for listings within the bounds, and returns Supercluster‑compatible GeoJSON clusters. In `src/lib/db.js` add a `getListingsInBounds(bounds)` helper that builds a parameterised query. In `server.js` register the new route and use the helper to return clusters. Update `src/components/MapView.jsx` to request clusters on map move/zoom, render cluster markers with count, and zoom into the cluster bounds on click. Ensure the existing listing markers still work when zoomed in.
acceptance: When the map is displayed, listings are grouped into cluster markers at low zoom levels; clicking a cluster zooms into its bounds and reveals individual listings.
The `/api/listings/cluster` endpoint returns correct GeoJSON with `cluster` and `point_count` properties for the current viewport and zoom, and the UI reflects these values without errors.

tasks.title: Google Calendar Sync for Listings
tasks.description: Implement OAuth2 flow to let hosts link a Google Calendar to a listing, fetch events via Google Calendar API, and store busy slots in the listings table (new columns `googleCalendarId` and `googleAccessToken`). Add a GraphQL mutation `linkGoogleCalendar(listingId: ID!, authCode: String!): Boolean` that exchanges the auth code for tokens, saves them, and triggers an initial sync. Extend the existing calendar sync job to also pull from Google Calendar for listings with a `googleCalendarId`. Update the ListingDetail component to show a "Connect Google Calendar" button, open the Google OAuth consent screen, and display sync status. Ensure that booking availability queries respect both iCal and Google Calendar busy slots.
acceptance: A host can click "Connect Google Calendar" on a listing, complete the OAuth flow, and see a success toast.
GraphQL query `listing(id: $id) { availability }` returns slots blocked according to events in the linked Google Calendar.

tasks.title: Visual Similarity Search for Listings
tasks.description: Add a visual similarity engine that generates image embeddings for each listing photo and stores them in the SQLite DB. Implement a new library module src/lib/imageEmbedding.js that uses a pre‑trained CLIP model (via @tensorflow/tfjs-node) to compute a 512‑dimensional vector for a given image. Extend src/lib/searchEngine.js with a function findSimilarListings(listingId, limit) that loads the target embedding and performs a cosine‑similarity query against all stored embeddings, returning the top N most similar listings. Update the GraphQL schema in server.js to expose a new query similarListings(listingId: ID!, limit: Int = 5): [Listing!]!. Modify src/components/ListingDetail.jsx to call this query after the listing loads and render a “Similar Listings” carousel using the existing ListingCard component. Ensure that when a new listing is created or its main photo is updated, the embedding is (‑computed and persisted.
acceptance: When a listing with a main photo is created, an embedding is stored in the DB and a console log confirms the vector length is 512.
Running the GraphQL query similarListings(listingId: "list_01", limit: 3) returns an array of up to three listings whose similarity scores are > 0.8 and the IDs are different from the source listing.
The ListingDetail page displays a “Similar Listings” carousel with at least one card for a listing that shares visual characteristics with the current listing.

Wrap all user‑visible strings in components with the t() function and replace hard‑coded text in src/components/**/*.jsx and src/App.jsx. Export the i18n instance for server‑side rendering support in server.js. Ensure the language selection persists in a cookie and defaults to English.

tasks.title: Interactive Map Clustering for Listings
tasks.description: Implement a server‑side clustering endpoint that returns listings grouped by geographic proximity using a quadtree algorithm. Add a new GraphQL query `clusteredListings(bbox: BoundingBox!, zoom: Int!): [Cluster]` in `src/lib/graphqlSchema.js` and resolver logic in `src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js`. Extend the Express server (`server.js`) to expose a `/api/map/cluster` REST endpoint that proxies the GraphQL query for legacy clients. On the frontend, create a new component `src/components/MapCluster.jsx` that fetches clusters, renders them with Leaflet markers, and expands a cluster into individual listings on click. Update `src/App.jsx` to import and display the component on the map view. Ensure the clustering respects the current map bounds and zoom level, and falls back to returning raw listings when zoom > 15.
acceptance: GET /api/map/cluster returns a JSON array of clusters with `lat`, `lng`, and `count` fields for zoom levels < 15 and individual listings for zoom >= 15.
MapCluster component renders markers that display the correct count and expands to show listing cards when a cluster marker is clicked.
